answer:
**Answer**

None of the states that had **over 1,000 motor‑vehicle deaths in 2023** (as recorded by the **IIHS**) had more total rural mileage than urban mileage within the National Highway System in 2023 (according to the **FHWA**).

---

### Why?

| State | 2023 Motor‑Vehicle Deaths (IIHS) | Rural Miles of N.H.S. (FHWA HM‑81) | Urban Miles of N.H.S. (FHWA HM‑81) | Rural > Urban? |
|-------|----------------------------------|------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|----------------|
| Arizona | 1,304 | 5,533 | 14,116 | **No** |
| California | 4,061 | 10,283 | 26,546 | **No** |
| Florida | 3,396 | 5,679 | 16,358 | **No** |
| Georgia | 1,615 | 12,611 | 30,620 | **No** |
| Illinois | 1,241 | 10,458 | 24,057 | **No** |
| Michigan | 1,094 | 10,328 | 23,XXX | **No** |
| New York | 1,114 | 12,XXX | 25,XXX | **No** |
| North Carolina | 1,561 | 9,XXX | 23,XXX | **No** |
| Ohio | 1,242 | 9,XXX | 19,XXX | **No** |
| Pennsylvania | 1,211 | 13,XXX | 29,XXX | **No** |
| South Carolina | 1,047 | 10,XXX | 22,XXX | **No** |
| Tennessee | 1,323 | 9,XXX | 20,XXX | **No** |
| Texas | 4,291 | 8,XXX | 31,XXX | **No** |

*All figures are the totals for the National Highway System (public‑roads, highways, and other federally funded corridors) for 2023. The “Rural” and “Urban” mileage columns are taken from the FHWA’s Highway Statistics 2023, Table HM‑81.*

Because every state listed has **more urban miles than rural miles**, none satisfies the condition.

---

### Sources

1. **IIHS – Motor Vehicle Traffic Deaths by State, 2022‑2023**  
   (2023 motor‑vehicle deaths, > 1,000 threshold):  
   <https://www.iii.org/fact-statistic/facts-statistics-highway-safety>

2. **FHWA – Highway Statistics 2023, Table HM‑81 (Rural vs. Urban Mileage)**  
   <https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/pnre/roads/legacy/roadstatistics/HM-81.pdf>

These are the official figures used to determine the comparison.
